title: Arhuaca mochila
about: Colombian artisan bag
blurb: The mochila arhuaca, or tutu iku in Ika, is a popular Colombian artisan bag made by the Arhuaco people of the Sierra Nevada. In recent years, they have become a cultural symbol of Colombian identity.

title: Backpack
blurb: A bag carried on both shoulders, from school corridors to mountain trails.

title: Bag
about: Flexible container
blurb: A bag, also known regionally as a sack or tote, is a common tool in the form of a floppy container, typically made of cloth, leather, bamboo, paper, or plastic.

title: Bandolier bag
about: Shoulder bag carried by Native Americans
blurb: A bandolier bag is a Native American shoulder pouch, often beaded. Early examples were made from pelts, twined fabrics, or hide, but beginning in the fur trade era, Native American women stitched bags of imported wool broadcloth, lined with cotton calico and often edged with silk ribbons.

title: Basket
about: Container woven of stiff fibres
blurb: A basket is a container that is traditionally constructed from stiff fibers, and can be made from a range of materials, including wood splints, runners, and cane. While most baskets are made from plant materials, other materials such as horsehair, baleen, or metal wire can be used.

title: Bayong
about: Filipino traditional bag
blurb: A bayong is a type of bag from the Philippines made by weaving dried leaves, usually from buri in the Visayas and pandan in Luzon. It is also made using native Philippine plants such as abaca, bacbac, karagumoy, sabutan, romblon and tikog.

title: Bindle
blurb: A bundle tied to the end of a stick and carried over the shoulder, the luggage of storybook wanderers.

title: Birkin bag
blurb: Hermès's hand-stitched leather tote, sketched on an aeroplane sick bag for Jane Birkin in 1984.

title: Bota bag
about: Traditional Spanish liquid receptacle
blurb: A bota bag is a traditional Spanish liquid receptacle, used mainly as a wineskin. It is often made out of leather, and is typically used to carry wine, although any liquid can be filled into it.

title: Briefcase
about: Narrow hard-sided box-shaped bag or case
blurb: A briefcase or an attaché case is a narrow hard-sided box-shaped bag or case used mainly for carrying papers and equipped with a handle.

title: Camera bag
about: Bag made for storing cameras or camera parts
blurb: Camera bags are a 20th-century development for the convenient carrying and quick access to high-end camera equipment. They replaced fitted leather cases that were supplied with the earliest cameras.

title: Canoe pack
about: Type of backpack designed for portages
blurb: A canoe pack, also known as a portage pack, is a specialized type of backpack used primarily where travel is largely by water punctuated by portages where the gear needs to be carried over land.

title: Carpet bag
about: Travel bag made from carpet or similar materials
blurb: A carpet bag is a top-opening travelling bag made of pile carpet, commonly from Brussels carpeting. It was a popular form of luggage in the United States and Europe in the 19th century, featuring simple handles and only an upper frame, which served as its closure.

title: Chanel 2.55
about: Luxury leather handbag
blurb: The Chanel 2.55 is a luxury leather handbag or purse designed by Coco Chanel and manufactured by the fashion house of Chanel.

title: Changing bag
about: Photographic bag designed to be light-proof
blurb: A changing bag is a photographic bag specifically designed to be light-proof and therefore to protect the light sensitive film before intended use. A changing bag is made of light proof material, and usually is composed of synthetic fibre.

title: Clutch
blurb: A small strapless handbag made to be held, big enough for keys, a phone and little else.

title: Coin purse
about: Small pouch made for carrying coins
blurb: A purse or pouch, sometimes called coin purse for clarity, is a small money bag or pouch, made for carrying coins. In most Commonwealth countries it is known simply as a purse, while "purse" in the United States usually refers to a handbag. An obsolete variant is a porte-monnaie.

title: Courtauld bag
about: Metal handbag believed to have been made in Mosul in the early 1300s
blurb: The "Courtauld bag" is a medieval handbag made of brass and inlaid with gold, silver, and an unidentified black material. Tentatively attributed to Mosul, sometime between 1300 and 1330 when it was ruled by the Ilkhanate, it is believed to be the oldest surviving handbag in the world.

title: Creel
about: Wicker basket used for carrying fish or blocks of peat
blurb: A creel is a wicker basket usually used for carrying fish or blocks of peat. It is also a fish trap used to catch lobsters and other crustaceans. In modern times, the term has come to encompass various types of wicker baskets used by anglers or commercial fishermen to hold fish or other prey.

title: Dillybag
about: Traditional Australian Aboriginal woven bag
blurb: A dillybag or dilly bag, also known as a mindirr or bulbbe, among other names, is a traditional Australian Aboriginal bag generally woven from plant fibres. Dillybags are mainly designed and used by women to gather and transport food, and are most commonly found in the northern parts of Australia.

title: Dior Saddle bag
about: Designer handbag by Dior
blurb: The Dior Saddle bag is a designer handbag introduced in 1999 by French fashion house Dior under the creative direction of John Galliano.

title: Dry bag
about: Type of flexible container
blurb: A dry bag is a type of flexible container which seals in a watertight manner. Dry bags are often used in kayaking, canoeing, rafting, canyoning, and other outdoor activities in which sensitive items would otherwise get wet, as well as extreme sports such as skiing and snowboarding.

title: Duffel bag
blurb: A cylindrical cloth holdall, named after the Belgian town whose thick cloth it was first made from.

title: Duluth pack
about: Specialized backpack used in canoe travel
blurb: A Duluth pack or Poirier pack is a traditional portage pack used in canoe travel, particularly in the Boundary Waters region of northern Minnesota and the Quetico Provincial Park of Ontario. It is a specialized type of backpack that is designed to fit in the bottom of canoes.

title: Fanny pack
blurb: A zipped pouch on a belt, worn at the waist or slung across the chest, forever going in and out of fashion.

title: Fjällräven Kånken
about: Backpack manufactured by Fjällräven
blurb: Kånken is a backpack sold by the Swedish outdoor equipment company Fjällräven. It is Fjällräven's best-known and best-selling product.

title: Flight bag
about: Document bag carried by pilots and flight crews
blurb: A flight bag can be any baggage taken on board a flight, but is usually a specific type of document bag carried by pilots and flight crews. Often adorned with an airline logo, at one time the flight bag was a chic fashion accessory.

title: Footlocker
about: Type of trunk or chest
blurb: A footlocker is a small trunk to be placed at the foot of a bed, used to store personal belongings. They can be secured by a padlock or combination lock, and are often used by soldiers or other military personnel.

title: Frakta
about: Bag manufactured by IKEA
blurb: The Frakta is a reusable tote bag manufactured by IKEA.

title: Furoshiki
blurb: A square Japanese wrapping cloth that knots into a bag for gifts, lunches or bottles.

title: Gaji bag
about: Large, open-topped hand bag
blurb: A gaji bag is a large, typically unfastened bag with parallel handles that emerge from the sides of its pouch. They are often used as reusable shopping bags. Gaji bags originated from the rural village of Jingliao in the Houbi District of Tainan, Taiwan during the Japanese colonial period.

title: Garment bag
about: Bag for carrying clothes
blurb: A garment bag or suit bag is a container of flexible material, usually used to ease transporting suits, jackets or clothing in general, and also to protect clothes from dust by hanging them inside with their hangers and then on a closet bar.

title: Gladstone bag
about: Small portmanteau suitcase
blurb: A Gladstone bag is a small portmanteau suitcase built over a rigid frame, which can separate into two equal sections. Gladstones are typically made of stiff leather and often belted with lanyards. The bags are named after William Gladstone, the four-time Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.

title: Hamper
about: Type of basket
blurb: A hamper refers to one of several related basket-like items. In primarily British usage, it refers to a wicker basket, usually large, that is used for the transport of items, often food.

title: Hand luggage
about: Luggage small enough to be carried in the passenger compartment of a vehicle
blurb: The term hand luggage or cabin baggage refers to the type of luggage that passengers are allowed to carry along in the passenger compartment of a vehicle instead of a separate cargo compartment.

title: Handbag
about: Handled bag used to carry personal items
blurb: A handbag, commonly known as a purse in North American English, is a handled medium-to-large bag used to carry personal items. It has also been called a pocketbook in parts of the U.S.

title: Haversack
about: Bag with a single shoulder strap
blurb: A haversack, musette bag, or small pack is a bag with a single shoulder strap. Although similar to a backpack, the single shoulder strap differentiates this type from other backpacks. There are exceptions to this general rule.

title: Hebao
about: Chinese embroidery pouches
blurb: Hebao, sometimes referred as Propitious pouch in English, is a generic term used to refer to Chinese embroidery pouches, purses, or small bags. When they are used as Chinese perfume pouch, they are referred to as Xiāngnáng, Xiāngbāo, or Xiāngdài. In everyday life, hebao are used to store items.

title: Hobo bag
about: Style of handbag
blurb: The hobo bag is a style of handbag or purse that is typically large and characterized by a crescent shape, a slouchy posture and a long strap designed to wear over the shoulder. Hobo bags are made out of soft, flexible materials and tend to slump, or slouch, when set down.

title: Hunting bag
about: Bag used by hunters to carry equipment
blurb: A hunting bag is a bag used by the hunter to transport their equipment, food and hunting accessories, e.g. cartridges, etc. It is usually medium sized, since it is also used to carry captured pieces.

title: Ita-bag
about: Handbag or backpack worn by anime or manga fans
blurb: An ita-bag is a handbag, backpack or other kind of bag covered in badges, buttons, figurines and other merchandise pertaining to anime and manga fandom. In Japan, ita-bags are a popular piece of apparel among female anime and manga fans.

title: JanSport
about: American backpack manufacturer
blurb: JanSport is an American brand of backpacks and collegiate apparel, now owned by VF Corporation, one of the world's largest apparel companies. JanSport is the world's largest backpack maker.

title: Kelly bag
blurb: The trapezoid Hermès handbag renamed after Grace Kelly used hers to shield herself from photographers.

title: Khorjin
about: Decorative carpet bag
blurb: A khorjin is a type of decorative carpet bag made across Greater Iran and Central Asia. Hand-knotted carpets and hand woven kilims were made by various nomadic tribes of the Middle East and Central Asia, including the Baloch, the Turkmen, the Afshars, the Bakhtyari, the Qashqai, and the Kurds,…

title: Kinchaku
about: Traditional Japanese drawstring bag
blurb: Kinchaku is a traditional Japanese drawstring bag, used like a handbag for carrying around personal possessions; smaller ones are usually used as sagemono, and used to carry small objects such as loose coinage, cosmetics, lucky charms, hand warmers and mobile phones.

title: Kiondo
about: Kenyan handwoven bag made from twine
blurb: A kiondo is a handwoven bag made from indigenous vegetable twine with leather trimmings. It is indigenous to the Taita, Kikuyu and Kamba tribes of Kenya. The Swahili word for a kiondoo is 'chondo,' plural 'vyondo'.

title: Medicine bag
about: Traditional North American Indian pouch
blurb: A medicine bag is usually a small pouch, worn by some Indigenous peoples of the Americas, that contains sacred items. A personal medicine bag may contain objects that symbolize personal well-being and tribal identity. Traditionally, medicine bags are worn under the clothing.

title: Messenger bag
blurb: A sack worn across the body on one strap, designed for couriers who needed their load at hand.

title: Money bag
about: Bag or sack used to hold money or gold
blurb: A money bag is a bag normally used to hold and transport coins and banknotes, often closed with a drawstring. When transported between banks and other institutions, money bags are usually moved in armored cars or money trains. It is a type of currency packaging.

title: Packing cube
about: Small bag for packing of clothes
blurb: A packing cube is a small bag designed to organize and compartmentalize clothes inside luggage, as well as to compress clothing to ensure optimum use of space. Packing cubes are used by backpackers, business travelers, and holidaymakers.

title: Pannier
about: One of a pair of baskets, bags, boxes, or similar containers
blurb: A pannier /ˈpæniər/ is a basket, bag, box, or similar container, carried in pairs either slung over the back of a beast of burden, or attached to the sides of a bicycle or motorcycle. The term derives from a Middle English borrowing of the Old French panier, meaning "bread basket".

title: Pasiking
about: Indigenous basket-backpack in the Philippines
blurb: The pasiking is the indigenous basket-backpack found among the various ethno-linguistic groups of Northern Luzon in the Philippines.

title: Portmanteau
about: Type of leather travelling bag
blurb: A portmanteau is a piece of luggage, usually made of leather and opening into two equal parts. Some are large, upright, and hinged at the back and enable hanging up clothes in one half, while others are much smaller bags with two equally sized compartments.

title: Punnet
about: Small box or square basket for fruits and vegetables
blurb: A punnet is a small box or square basket for the gathering, transport and sale of fruit and vegetables, typically for small berries susceptible to bruising, spoiling and squashing that are therefore best kept in small rigid containers.

title: Purse accessories
about: Fashion accessories for handbags
blurb: Purse accessories are fashion accessories that are made specifically for handbags, to enhance their functionality or appearance.

title: Randoseru
about: Japanese school backpack
blurb: A randoseru is a firm-sided backpack made of stitched firm leather or leather-like synthetic material, most commonly used in Japan by elementary schoolchildren. Traditionally it is given to a child upon beginning their first year of school, whereupon the child uses the same bag until grade 6.

title: Red-white-blue bag
about: Nylon carry bag associated with Hong Kong culture
blurb: Red-white-blue bag or laundry bag is a carriage bag made out of nylon canvas in colors of red, white and blue. It originated in Hong Kong in the 1960s and has become a representative of Hong Kong culture.

title: Reticule
about: Small handbag, originally with a drawstring closure, and often decorated with beadwork
blurb: A reticule, also known as a ridicule or indispensable, was a type of small handbag or purse, similar to a modern evening bag, used mainly from 1795 to 1820. The reticule became popular with the advent of Regency fashions in the late 18th century.

title: Sabretache
about: Flat bag of cavalry soldiers
blurb: A sabretache is a flat bag or pouch, which was worn suspended from the belt of a cavalry soldier together with the sabre.

title: Saddlebag
about: Bag attached to a saddle
blurb: Saddlebags are bags that are attached to saddles.

title: Samsonite
about: Luxembourg luggage manufacturer
blurb: Samsonite International S.A. is a Luxembourg-based multinational luggage manufacturer and retailer, with products ranging from large suitcases to small toiletries, bags and briefcases. The company was founded in 1910 in Denver, Colorado, United States.

title: Satchel
blurb: A flap-topped leather bag with a long strap, the classic school bag of British storybooks.

title: Schultüte
about: Kind of bag that is delivered in Germany to students on the first day of school
blurb: A Schultüte, also known as a Zuckertüte in some parts of Germany, is a large cone-shaped, cornucopia-styled container made of paper, cardboard, or plastic.

title: Shell purse
about: Type of purse made from shells
blurb: A shell purse is a type of coin purse that is made from whole or trimmed mollusk shells, especially from bivalve mollusc shells. These purses are of mainly novelty use and purchased as souvenirs of visits, etc.

title: Showbag
about: Themed bag of items often sold at Australian agricultural shows
blurb: A showbag is a themed bag of commercial products, novelty items and promotional merchandise, usually made available for purchase. It is a distinctive feature of Australian agricultural shows, where they are sold from stalls; they can also be found at exhibitions, festivals and fundraising events.

title: Skirt-bag
about: Hybrid fashion item made by Ivana Barač
blurb: Skirt-bag - a hybrid fashion design item made by Ivana Barač presented in 2008 in Kino EUROPA, Zagreb, Croatia. Design is not a common baggy skirt design, but a specific dual function item with exceptional construction.

title: Sporran
about: Belt pouch traditionally worn with men's Scottish Highland dress
blurb: The sporran, a traditional part of male Scottish Highland dress, is a pouch that functions as a pocket for the kilt. Made of leather or fur, the ornamentation of the sporran is chosen to complement the formality of dress worn with it.

title: Steamer trunk
blurb: A large travel chest from the age of ocean liners, plastered with hotel labels.

title: Stuff sack
about: Drawstring bag usually used for camping items
blurb: A stuff sack is a type of drawstring bag, usually used for storing camping items. Stuff sacks are commonly used for the storage of sleeping bags, which are then stuffed into the bag, rather than rolled or folded.

title: Suitcase
about: Form of luggage
blurb: A suitcase is a form of baggage. It is a rectangular container with a handle and is typically used to carry one's clothes and other belongings while traveling.

title: Sutton Hoo purse-lid
about: Anglo-Saxon archaeological object found in Suffolk, England
blurb: The Sutton Hoo purse-lid is one of the major objects excavated from the Anglo-Saxon royal burial-ground at Sutton Hoo in Suffolk, England.

title: Toiletry bag
about: Portable container that holds hygiene and toiletry supplies
blurb: A toiletry bag is a portable container—usually a pouch with a drawstring or zippered closure—that holds body hygiene and toiletry supplies such as toothbrush and toothpaste, dental floss, cotton swabs, deodorant, nail clippers, tweezers, soap, shaving supplies, hairbrush, contact lenses and…

title: Tote bag
blurb: A big open bag with two parallel handles, usually canvas, usually carrying more than intended.

title: Train case
about: Piece of luggage
blurb: A train case is a piece of luggage, used especially for personal grooming articles, usually smaller and boxlike. Nécessaire de voyage predate train cases but contain similar tools, such as brushes, and consumables, such as cosmetics.

title: Tumi Inc.
about: American suitcase and bag manufacturer
blurb: Tumi Holdings, Inc., is a manufacturer of high-end suitcases and bags for travel based in Edison, New Jersey. It was a unit of Doughty Hanson & Co. from 2004 until after its 2012 initial public offering, which preceded its acquisition by Samsonite in 2016.

title: Vera Bradley
about: American luggage and handbag design company
blurb: Vera Bradley Sales, LLC is an American travel gear design company, founded by Barbara Bradley Baekgaard and Patricia R. Miller in 1982. As of 2026, its home office is in Roanoke, Indiana. The company was named after Baekgaard's mother.

title: Wallet
about: Flat case or pouch used to carry small personal items
blurb: A wallet is a flat case or pouch, often used to carry small personal items such as physical currency, debit cards, and credit cards; identification documents such as driving licence, identification card, club card; photographs, transit pass, business cards and other paper or laminated cards.
